added_failure_note: the reviewed run recorded no baseline arm (its manifest carries neither baseline_suite nor after_suite); its only suite log is the focused gate at after-suite.log, which ends 168 passed, 2 skipped, EXIT=0 with zero FAILED ids, so no failure id is added on the evidence that exists and none could be added on an arm that was not run.

findings.text: this file, tests/standard_names/test_failed_source_reason.py:142 and tests/standard_names/test_generate_name_persist.py:537 were edited outside the declared write paths, so the node's declared fence does not describe the change; the edits are small stub and statement-count updates forced by the new append and are disclosed in the manifest's outside_scope field, but the fence was never extended to cover them.

nothing asserts that _orphan_sweep_tick issues the capped append: test_attempt_cap_disposition.py:125 answers a StandardNameSourceClaimAttempt query but no test reads stub.queries for it, so deleting this call leaves all 23 node tests green and the capped outcome silently stops being recorded on the sweep path.

the fragment states the receipt and the ending are one unit of work, but only the produced append at graph_source_bindings.py:1708 runs inside the ending transaction; the stored-status, released and capped appends are separate autocommit statements issued before an ending statement that can still match no row, so the claim is true of one of five writers and a reader auditing durability is misled.

the fragment says a sweep-parked source carries no live sequence and is keyed on attempt-N, but orphan_sweep.py:130-135 returns s.claim_seq and does not clear it, so _capped_claim_entries keys the receipt on the sequence and the attempt-keyed form is reached only when claim_seq is null, which is the case only test_an_unclaimed_source_keys_its_receipt_on_the_attempt exercises.

item.get('claim_outcome') is read as an override but no writer in the repository sets that key, so the branch is dead and the outcome is decided solely by the status map, which hides from a reader that a caller could once have overridden it and is untested by the parametrised status tests.

the relationship table enumerates every StandardNameSource edge including HAS_RETRY_EVENT but not the new HAS_CLAIM_ATTEMPT, so the repository's own graph map omits the relationship this node adds; the file is outside the node's write scope, so the omission could not be repaired here and needs a home in a later node.
